## Recovered nonzero timing within the declared frontier

The previous intrinsic division rule extends to the captured finite non-whole
literal operands without rounding/replacing nonzero quotient payloads. Keep
constant-literal provenance, known valid typed metadata, magnitude<1e10,
divisor magnitude>=1, real scale0..18/full width<=31/whole width<=12, Integer
payload/width bounds and checked arithmetic. Small constant divisors, unknown
producers and wider/nonfinite inputs remain mandatory follow-ons. Integer
storage still requires BOTH input storage tags Integer and an in-range integral
quotient; equal numeric payloads do not infer storage or origin.

Use intrinsic scale=min(18,DL+DR), left whole-width and quotient/sign digits as
in the earlier intrinsic contract; preserve the existing integral-storage and
constant-zero behavior. Prepare the DECIMALS floor when the constant node is
evaluated. Grouping and folded-child division keep intrinsic attributes; unary
minus consumes intrinsic precision, while runtime-return negation sees the
materialized value. Runtime arguments and mixed division consume the prepared
descriptor, not a post-callback setting read. Ungrouped completed prefixes must
survive continuation just like grouped operands, without replaying user code.

For example, at initial D14 `(0.5/2)/CFMark(0)` is realW17/D14, whereas
`-((0.5/2))/CFMark(0)` is realW6/D2. The callback occurs once and leaves D0.
`CFMark(0)/(0.5/2)` is realW5/D2, because its right operand is evaluated later.
`0.5/2/CFMark(0)` retains the same prepared D14 as the grouped left operand.
These are native complete-expression observations, not separately evaluated
child descriptors treated as folded-child oracles.

The retained post-capture candidate initially mispredicted168 LPARAMETERS
widths by carrying the positive-scale width11+D formula into D0. Actual native
real D0 parameter width is10 plus sign; positive scales include the point.
The rejected source/result are preserved. Correcting that candidate-only
normalization yields zero differences across2,220 nonzero observations, including
